operation_details.item: The user uses MongoDB for one of the storage layers.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Let's review the storage architecture for the service and make sure the design notes reflect the current implementation.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I use Postgres for the primary database.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Understood. We can treat that as the main source of relational data and focus the review on the supporting layers.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That gives us a clear separation between durable application data and fast-access cached data. What other persistence needs should the architecture capture?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I use MongoDB for one of the storage layers.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: We should document why that layer is separate from the primary database, including its data shape, access patterns, and consistency expectations.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Storage choices are listed in the system design doc.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Great. I would review that section alongside the service boundaries and make sure operational responsibilities are explicit.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I want the implementation review to focus on how the services select the appropriate storage layer rather than on stylistic refactoring.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That makes sense. We can trace representative read and write paths, check failure handling, and compare the code with the documented architecture.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: The next step is to walk through those paths and identify any mismatches between the running system and the design documentation.
